A.question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람의 반 티셔츠 디자인으로 가장 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Emma, is that the design for our class T-shirt?
W: Yes. We'll wear it on sports day. Look, there's a lion on the front.
M: Cool. Is our class number under the lion?
W: No, it's on the back. And the T-shirt is yellow.
M: Yellow? I thought we chose white.
W: We did, but white gets dirty too fast.
choices: 흰 티셔츠 앞면에 사자가 있고, 반 번호는 뒷면에 있는 디자인
노란 티셔츠 앞면에 사자가 있고, 반 번호는 뒷면에 있는 디자인
노란 티셔츠 앞면에 사자가 있고, 그 아래에 반 번호가 있는 디자인
노란 티셔츠 앞면에 별이 있고, 반 번호는 뒷면에 있는 디자인
A.explain_ko: 앞면에 사자, 반 번호는 뒷면, 색은 흰색에서 노란색으로 바뀌었다. 흰색·사자 아래 번호는 대화에서 나왔다가 아니라고 한 것이다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람의 관계로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Hello. Are you here for a family photo?
W: Yes. It's for my grandma's seventieth birthday.
M: Great. Please sit here, and your brother can stand behind you.
W: Like this? Should I take off my glasses?
M: No, they look nice. Now, everyone, look at the camera and smile.
W: Did my brother close his eyes?
M: Yes, he did. Let's take one more.
A.explain_ko: 가족사진을 찍으러 온 손님에게 자리를 잡아 주고 카메라를 보라고 하므로 사진사와 손님이다. 안경·할머니는 대화에 나온 말로 만든 오답이다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 심정으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Tom, you look down. What's wrong?
M: My family was going to go fishing at the river this Saturday, but my dad has to work.
W: Oh, that's too bad. You were looking forward to it.
M: Yes. I wanted to catch a really big fish this time.
W: Maybe you can go next weekend.
M: Wait, my dad just sent me a message. He doesn't have to work after all!
W: Really? So you can go?
M: Yes! And my uncle is bringing his boat. I can't wait!
A.explain_ko: 처음에는 낚시를 못 가서 실망했지만, 아빠가 일하지 않아도 된다는 소식에 삼촌 배까지 타게 되어 마지막에는 신이 났다. '실망한'은 처음 심정이다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 남자에게 부탁한 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Sam, the students from Canada are visiting our school this Friday.
M: I know. Our class is having a welcome party for them, right?
W: Yes. Emily is drawing a big welcome sign, and Mr. Hall will bring snacks.
M: What about name tags?
W: Jason and I are making them tonight. But we still need someone to take photos at the party.
M: I have a good camera at home.
W: Great. Can you do it for us? We want to make a photo book for them.
M: Sure. I'll bring my camera on Friday.
A.explain_ko: 여자는 파티에서 사진 찍을 사람이 필요하다며 카메라가 있는 남자에게 부탁했다. 표지판은 Emily, 간식은 Mr. Hall, 이름표는 여자와 Jason이 맡았다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Dad, I'm going to bake banana bread for Grandpa's visit tomorrow.
M: Sounds great, Olivia. Do you have a recipe?
W: Yes, but I want to make it my own way. I'll use honey instead of sugar and add some chocolate chips.
M: Is this your first time making banana bread?
W: Yes. Why?
M: When you try a recipe for the first time, I think you should follow it exactly. Then you'll know how it's supposed to taste. If you change many things at once and the bread fails, you won't know what went wrong. Next time, you can change one thing and see the difference.
W: Okay. I'll use sugar this time.
choices: 설탕 대신 꿀을 넣으면 더 건강한 빵을 만들 수 있다.
처음 만드는 요리는 요리법을 그대로 따라 해야 한다.
손님이 오는 날에는 처음 해 보는 요리를 하지 않는 것이 좋다.
요리를 잘하려면 여러 재료를 한꺼번에 바꿔 보아야 한다.
A.explain_ko: 아빠는 처음 해 보는 요리법은 그대로 따라 해야 맛이 어때야 하는지 알고, 한꺼번에 여러 가지를 바꾸면 무엇이 잘못됐는지 모른다고 한다. 꿀·설탕, 할아버지 방문은 대화에 나온 말로 만든 오답이다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자의 마지막 말에 이어질 남자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Excuse me. Do you have these hiking boots in size nine?
W: Let me check our stock. I'm sorry, but size nine is sold out in brown.
M: Oh no. My family is going hiking in the mountains this week. I really need new boots.
W: I can order a pair for you. They'll arrive on Friday.
M: Friday is too late. We're leaving on Wednesday morning.
W: I see. Well, we have the same boots in size nine, but in gray. Would you like to try them on?
choices: Great. I'll pick them up on Friday, then.
No problem. I'll wait until the brown ones arrive.
Sure. The color isn't important to me.
Thanks, but size nine is too big for me.
A.explain_ko: 갈색은 금요일에나 오는데 수요일에 떠나야 하므로, 같은 치수의 회색을 신어 보겠다는 응답이 알맞다. 금요일에 찾으러 오겠다는 말은 떠나는 날 뒤라 맞지 않는다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 전화한 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script:
M: Hello, Brush and Color Art Studio. This is Mark speaking.
W: Hi, Mark. This is Karen Wells. My son Tyler takes your watercolor class on Tuesdays.
M: Oh, yes. Tyler is doing really well. His painting of the harbor last week was wonderful.
W: Thank you. He loves your class. Actually, that's why I'm calling. Starting next month, he has swimming practice on Tuesdays, but he doesn't want to give up painting.
M: I see. We have the same watercolor class on Thursdays at four thirty.
W: That would be perfect. Is there any space in that class?
M: Yes, there are two spots left. Should I move him to Thursdays from next month?
W: Yes, please. And does he need to bring anything new?
M: No, the same brushes and paper will be fine.
choices: 아들의 그림을 칭찬해 준 것에 감사하려고
A.explain_ko: 화요일에 수영 연습이 생겨 아들의 수채화 수업을 목요일로 옮기려고 전화했다. 칭찬·수영·준비물은 대화 중에 곁들여 나온 이야기다.

A.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
A.script:
W: Hi. I'd like to buy some souvenirs for my friends back home.
M: Sure. These keychains are very popular. They're five dollars each.
W: They're cute. I'll take four. And how much is this mug with the lighthouse on it?
M: It's fifteen dollars. If you buy two mugs, the second one is half price.
W: I only need one. It's for my aunt.
M: Okay. Anything else?
W: What about these postcards?
M: They're one dollar each, but they're free if you spend thirty dollars or more.
W: Great. Then I'll take three postcards, too. Oh, wait. My friend Jake already has a keychain like this. I'll take three keychains, not four.
M: No problem. So, three keychains, one mug, and three postcards.
W: That's right. Here's my card.
A.explain_ko: 열쇠고리 3개 $15 + 머그 1개 $15 = $30이고, $30 이상이라 엽서 3장은 무료다. $35는 열쇠고리 4개로 계산한 값, $33은 엽서 값을 더한 값이다.

A.question: 다음을 듣고, 학교 앨범 사진 촬영에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
A.script: M: Hello, everyone. This is Nathan Hughes, your student council president. I'd like to tell you about Yearbook Photo Day. Photos for this year's yearbook will be taken next Tuesday and Wednesday in the school auditorium. First-year students will have their photos taken on Tuesday, and second- and third-year students will have theirs taken on Wednesday. Please wear your school uniform, and don't forget your name tag. Each photo takes only about two minutes, so your homeroom teacher will send you there in small groups during class time. If you are absent on your day, you can come to the make-up session next Monday after school. Also, the photographers will take a group photo of every club on Thursday at lunchtime. Club leaders should sign up at the student council room by this Friday. Thank you.
choices: 동아리 단체 사진은 목요일 방과 후에 찍는다.
결석한 학생은 다음 주 월요일 방과 후에 찍을 수 있다.
A.explain_ko: 동아리 단체 사진은 목요일 점심시간에 찍는다. '방과 후'는 결석자 보충 촬영(월요일)에 나온 말이다.

A.question:
다음 표를 보면서 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 예약할 고래 관찰 투어를 고르시오.
투어 | 출발 시각 | 걸리는 시간 | 1인 가격 | 점심
A | 8:00 | 3시간 | $45 | 없음
B | 9:30 | 4시간 | $60 | 있음
C | 10:00 | 2시간 | $40 | 없음
D | 1:00 (오후) | 4시간 | $55 | 있음
A.script:
W: Honey, let's book a whale-watching tour for the last day of our trip. Here are four tours.
M: Great. The kids will love it. Look, the eight o'clock tour is cheap.
W: Eight? Remember how hard it was to wake the kids up yesterday? I don't think we can make it.
M: You're right. Then how about the ten o'clock one? It's the cheapest of all.
W: But it's only two hours long. The hotel staff told me the whales usually stay far from the shore, so we need at least three hours.
M: Okay. Then we have two choices left. The nine thirty tour includes lunch.
W: It does, but it costs too much. We said we'd spend no more than fifty-five dollars per person.
M: Then this one is perfect. It includes lunch, too.
W: Good. Let's book it now.
A.explain_ko: 8시 출발(A)은 아이들이 못 일어나서, 2시간짜리(C)는 너무 짧아서, 1인 $60(B)은 예산 $55를 넘어서 빠진다. 남는 것은 D다.

A.question: 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script: W: Hello, listeners. This is Rebecca Stone with Family on the Road. When parents plan a family vacation, they usually decide everything themselves: where to stay, what to see, and where to eat. Then they wonder why their children look bored in the back seat. Here's my suggestion. Give each child one part of the trip to plan. A ten-year-old can choose the restaurant for one dinner. A teenager can research a museum and decide which rooms the family will visit first. Of course, you can set a budget and a few simple rules. But once the choice is made, try to follow it, even if it isn't what you would pick. Children who plan part of a trip pay more attention, ask more questions, and remember the places much longer. Their small decisions turn them from passengers into real travelers. So on your next vacation, share the map.
choices: 가족 여행의 예산과 규칙은 부모가 미리 정해 두어야 한다.
자녀와 여행할 때는 박물관처럼 배울 것이 많은 곳을 골라야 한다.
여행 일정은 여유 있게 짜서 자녀가 지루하지 않게 해야 한다.
가족 여행 계획의 일부를 자녀에게 맡기면 자녀가 여행에 더 깊이 참여한다.
A.explain_ko: 아이마다 여행의 한 부분을 계획하게 하면 더 집중하고 오래 기억한다는 것이 요지다. 예산·규칙, 박물관은 예로 든 세부 내용이다.

A.question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Grace가 Owen에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
A.script: W: Grace and her classmate Owen meet every Saturday at a café near their school to study for their chemistry exam. They usually study there from ten until two. The café used to be quiet, but last month a music class started next door, and now it gets very noisy after eleven. Owen suggests moving to the city library, but Grace knows that all of the library's study rooms are booked for the whole month. Then she remembers that her aunt's bakery is closed on Saturdays, and there is a large table in the back room. She calls her aunt, and her aunt says they are welcome to use it. So Grace wants to suggest to Owen that they study at the bakery from next Saturday. In this situation, what would Grace most likely say to Owen?
choices: How about studying in the back room of my aunt's bakery from next week?
Why don't we book a study room at the city library?
Let's come to the café earlier, before the music class starts.
Could you ask the music teacher to keep the noise down?
A.explain_ko: 도서관 스터디룸은 한 달 내내 예약이 차 있고, 이모가 토요일에 쉬는 빵집 뒷방을 써도 된다고 했으므로 그곳에서 공부하자고 제안한다. 일찍 와도 2시까지 공부하므로 소음을 피할 수 없다.

A.passage: Today is Art Day at my school, so we do not have math or English. We paint pictures all morning. I paint my dog, and my friend Mina paints the sea. Our teacher puts __them__ on the wall.
A.question: What does Mina paint?
A.explain_ko: my friend Mina paints the sea → 바다를 그린다.

A.passage: Today is Art Day at my school, so we do not have math or English. We paint pictures all morning. I paint my dog, and my friend Mina paints the sea. Our teacher puts __them__ on the wall.
A.question: What does __them__ mean?
A.explain_ko: 선생님이 벽에 붙이는 것은 우리가 그린 그림(pictures)이다.

A.passage: I have a small hamster, and his name is Bobo. He sleeps all day and plays at night. At night, he runs on his wheel and eats seeds. I love Bobo very much.
A.question: What is the story about?
choices: a new wheel for my bike
A.explain_ko: 글 전체가 햄스터 Bobo 이야기이다.

A.passage: I have a small hamster, and his name is Bobo. He sleeps all day and plays at night. At night, he runs on his wheel and eats seeds. I love Bobo very much.
A.question: When does Bobo sleep?
A.explain_ko: He sleeps all day → 낮 동안 잔다.

A.passage: Hana took a paper-making class at the community center. She tore old newspapers into small pieces. She put them in warm water and mixed them into a thick soup. She spread the soup on a screen and pressed the water out. The next day, the paper was _____, so Hana wrote a card on it.
A.question: Which word best fits in the blank?
A.explain_ko: 다음 날 종이가 말라서(dry) 그 위에 카드를 쓸 수 있었다.

A.passage: Hana took a paper-making class at the community center. She tore old newspapers into small pieces. She put them in warm water and mixed them into a thick soup. She spread the soup on a screen and pressed the water out. The next day, the paper was _____, so Hana wrote a card on it.
A.question: What did Hana put in the warm water?
A.explain_ko: She tore old newspapers into small pieces. She put them in warm water.

A.passage: The clock on the old tower in Saebit Town stopped last month. People looked up and saw the wrong time. So Mr. Yoon, a clock repairman, climbed up the tower. He cleaned the inside of the clock and changed a broken part. It took him three days. Now the clock rings every hour again.
A.question: What is the best title for the story?
choices: A New Tower for the Town
A.explain_ko: 멈춘 마을 시계탑의 시계를 고친 이야기이다.

A.passage: The clock on the old tower in Saebit Town stopped last month. People looked up and saw the wrong time. So Mr. Yoon, a clock repairman, climbed up the tower. He cleaned the inside of the clock and changed a broken part. It took him three days. Now the clock rings every hour again.
A.question: Which is true about the story?
choices: Mr. Yoon built a new tower.
Mr. Yoon fixed the clock in three days.
The clock rings only in the morning.
A.explain_ko: It took him three days. 멈춘 때는 지난달, 탑은 그대로, 시계는 매시간 울린다.

A.passage:
Dear students,
Next Friday is Career Day at Hanbit Elementary School. A firefighter, Ms. Park, will visit our school. She will tell you about her job and show you her fire truck. You can also try on her helmet and ask her questions. Please come to the playground at 10 a.m. Don't forget to bring a pencil and a notebook. Thank you!
A.question: Why did the writer write this?
choices: to tell students about a firefighter's visit
to ask students to become firefighters
to thank a firefighter for her help
to tell students about a fire at school
A.explain_ko: 소방관이 학교에 온다는 것을 알리는 안내문이다.

A.passage:
Dear students,
Next Friday is Career Day at Hanbit Elementary School. A firefighter, Ms. Park, will visit our school. She will tell you about her job and show you her fire truck. You can also try on her helmet and ask her questions. Please come to the playground at 10 a.m. Don't forget to bring a pencil and a notebook. Thank you!
A.question: What should students bring?
A.explain_ko: Don't forget to bring a pencil and a notebook.

A.passage: Minho joined the school table tennis club this spring. At first, he could not hit the ball well. It often went into the net, and some friends laughed. But Minho did not _____. He practiced for an hour every day after school. His coach helped him, too. After two months, he won his first game. Now he is one of the best players in the club.
A.question: Which is NOT true about Minho?
choices: He joined the club this spring.
He practiced every day after school.
His coach did not help him.
He won a game after two months.
A.explain_ko: His coach helped him, too. → 코치가 도와주었다.

A.passage: Minho joined the school table tennis club this spring. At first, he could not hit the ball well. It often went into the net, and some friends laughed. But Minho did not _____. He practiced for an hour every day after school. His coach helped him, too. After two months, he won his first game. Now he is one of the best players in the club.
A.question: Which best fits in the blank?
A.explain_ko: 친구들이 웃었지만 포기하지 않고(give up) 매일 연습했다.

A.passage: Have you ever looked at your shadow at different times of the day? In the morning, the sun is low in the sky, so your shadow is long. At noon, the sun is high above your head. Then your shadow becomes very short. In the late afternoon, the sun goes down again, and your shadow grows _____. Long ago, people used shadows like a clock. They put a stick in the ground and watched its shadow move. So a shadow can tell us the time of day.
A.question: 이 글의 주제로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 하루 동안 그림자 길이가 바뀌는 까닭과 그 쓰임
A.explain_ko: 해의 높이에 따라 그림자 길이가 바뀌고, 옛사람들은 이것을 시계처럼 썼다.

A.passage: Have you ever looked at your shadow at different times of the day? In the morning, the sun is low in the sky, so your shadow is long. At noon, the sun is high above your head. Then your shadow becomes very short. In the late afternoon, the sun goes down again, and your shadow grows _____. Long ago, people used shadows like a clock. They put a stick in the ground and watched its shadow move. So a shadow can tell us the time of day.
A.question: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
A.explain_ko: 해가 다시 낮아지면 아침처럼 그림자가 길어진다(longer).

A.passage:
Last weekend, my family visited Jungang Market, an old market in our town.
(A) After lunch, we walked to the other side of the market. There, an old man was making wooden toys by hand. My little brother bought a small wooden horse from __him__.
(B) First, we went to the food street. There were many small shops selling hot rice cakes, fish cakes, and dumplings. We sat down at a tiny table and ate lunch there.
(C) Before we went home, Mom bought some fresh fruit. It was a long but happy day.
A.question: 주어진 첫 문장 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 알맞은 것은?
A.explain_ko: First(B) → After lunch(A) → Before we went home(C).

A.passage:
Last weekend, my family visited Jungang Market, an old market in our town.
(A) After lunch, we walked to the other side of the market. There, an old man was making wooden toys by hand. My little brother bought a small wooden horse from __him__.
(B) First, we went to the food street. There were many small shops selling hot rice cakes, fish cakes, and dumplings. We sat down at a tiny table and ate lunch there.
(C) Before we went home, Mom bought some fresh fruit. It was a long but happy day.
A.question: 밑줄 친 __him__ 이 가리키는 사람은?
A.explain_ko: 남동생은 나무 장난감을 만들던 노인(an old man)에게서 말을 샀다.

A.passage: Every day, at the same times, weather stations around the world send big balloons high into the sky. These weather balloons are filled with a gas that is lighter than air, so they rise quickly. Each balloon carries a small box with tools inside. As it goes up, the box measures the temperature and how wet the air is. Then it sends this information back to the ground. The air gets thinner higher up, so the balloon slowly grows bigger. At about thirty kilometers, it becomes as big as a small house and finally pops. The box falls back to Earth with a small parachute. Scientists use the information to tell us tomorrow's weather.
A.question: 이 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: How to Make a Paper Balloon
Why the Air Is Getting Dirty
The Tallest House in the World
Weather Balloons: Helpers in the Sky
A.explain_ko: 날씨 풍선이 하늘로 올라가며 날씨 정보를 모으는 과정을 설명하는 글이다.

A.passage: Every day, at the same times, weather stations around the world send big balloons high into the sky. These weather balloons are filled with a gas that is lighter than air, so they rise quickly. Each balloon carries a small box with tools inside. As it goes up, the box measures the temperature and how wet the air is. Then it sends this information back to the ground. The air gets thinner higher up, so the balloon slowly grows bigger. At about thirty kilometers, it becomes as big as a small house and finally pops. The box falls back to Earth with a small parachute. Scientists use the information to tell us tomorrow's weather.
A.question: 이 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 풍선에는 공기보다 가벼운 기체가 들어 있다.
풍선에 달린 상자가 기온과 공기 속 물기를 잰다.
상자는 작은 낙하산을 달고 땅으로 떨어진다.
A.explain_ko: the balloon slowly grows bigger → 올라갈수록 점점 커진다.

A.passage:
Dear Mayor Choi,
I am writing to you as a student at Daehan Middle School. My name is Seojin Park. Every day, about fifty students ride bikes to our school. Riding a bike is healthy, and it does not make the air dirty. However, the road in front of our school is very dangerous. Cars and buses drive fast there, and there is no special road for bikes. Last month, one of my friends almost had an accident. I am writing to ask you to make a safe bike lane on this road. Then more students will ride bikes, and everyone will be safer. Thank you for reading my letter.
Sincerely,
Seojin Lee
A.question: 이 글을 쓴 목적으로 가장 알맞은 것은?

친구가 사고를 당할 뻔한 일을 전하려고
학교에 자전거 보관대를 늘려 달라고 부탁하려고
A.explain_ko: I am writing to ask you to make a safe bike lane on this road.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 두 사람이 대화하는 장소로 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.

W: Of course. Here you are.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 대화 직후에 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

W: Jake, what's that poster?

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
B.script:
M: Excuse me. How do I use these machines? It's my first time at this laundromat.
W: Sure. The washing machines are four dollars, and the dryers are three dollars.
M: I have a lot of clothes, so I need two washing machines.
W: Then you'll need two dryers, too. But the big dryer is only five dollars, and it can dry both loads.
M: Great. I'll use the big one. Do I need to buy soap?
W: It's one dollar a box, but you can use your own.
M: I brought my own. Thanks.
B.explain_ko: 세탁기 2대 $8 + 큰 건조기 1대 $5 = $13. 비누는 가져와서 사지 않는다. $14는 건조기 2대, $15는 건조기 2대와 비누, $9는 세탁기 1대.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 남자에게 부탁한 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

W: Ethan, are you busy this Saturday morning?

B.question: 다음을 듣고, Pine Valley Chalk Art Day에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.

To join, please sign up on the town website by October fifth. The best three drawings will appear on the town calendar next year.

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 마지막 말에 대한 여자의 응답으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

B.question: 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script: M: Good afternoon, residents of Cedar Hills. This is Paul Grant from the town environment team. Every year, our town throws away tons of things like toasters, lamps, and torn jackets. But many of them are not really broken. They just need a small fix. So we're starting the Cedar Hills Repair Café. On the first Sunday of every month, volunteers who are good at fixing things will be at the town hall from one to five. Bring your broken items, and they will repair them with you for free. You can also learn how to fix things by yourself. Let's give our old things a second life and make less trash together. We hope to see you there.
choices: 마을 회관 운영 시간 변경을 알리려고
고장 난 물건을 무료로 함께 고쳐 주는 수리 카페를 알리려고

B.question: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
B.script:
M: Welcome to the Sky Valley Balloon Festival. How can I help you?
W: Hi. I'd like to buy tickets for the balloon ride for my family.
M: Sure. Tickets are forty dollars for adults and twenty-five dollars for children under twelve.
W: There are two adults and two children. My daughter is eight, and my son is thirteen.
M: Then your son needs an adult ticket. So that's three adult tickets and one child ticket.
W: I see. I have a coupon from the festival website. Can I use it?
M: Let me see. This coupon gives you ten percent off, but only on adult tickets.
W: That's fine. Also, can we get a photo of our family in the balloon?
M: Yes. A printed photo is ten dollars.
W: Great. I'll take one photo.
B.explain_ko: 13세 아들은 어른 요금 → 어른 3장 $120의 10% 할인 $108 + 어린이 1장 $25 + 사진 $10 = $143. $133은 사진 뺌, $155는 할인 뺌, $132는 아들을 어린이로 셈.

B.question: 다음을 듣고, 방송 동아리 On Air의 신입 회원 모집에 관해 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
B.script: W: Good morning, everyone. I'm Hannah Wells, the president of On Air, our school's radio club. We're looking for new members for this semester. Don't worry if you have no experience. Senior members will teach you how to use the equipment during a two-week training period. We'll choose six new members this year. If you're interested, send us a one-minute recording of yourself introducing your favorite song. The deadline is next Friday, and we'll announce the results on the school website. Come and make your voice heard!
B.explain_ko: 모집 인원(6명), 지원 방법(1분 녹음 파일), 교육 기간(2주)은 말했지만 동아리실이 어디인지는 말하지 않았다.

B.question:

아르바이트 | 요일 | 시급 | 가는 방법

B.question: 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script: M: Hello, listeners. This is Coach Ryan Mitchell with Fit for Life. Have you ever stopped exercising for a few weeks because of a cold, exams, or a busy schedule? When people come back, they often try to start exactly where they stopped. If they used to run five kilometers, they run five kilometers on the first day. But after a break, your muscles, heart, and lungs are not at the same level as before. Pushing them too hard can lead to injuries or make you so sore that you give up again. So when you return, begin with about half of what you used to do. Then add a little more each week and listen to your body. It may feel slow, but it's the safest way to get back to your old level. Remember, the goal is not one great workout but a habit you can keep.
choices: 운동 전에는 반드시 충분히 몸을 풀어야 한다.
감기에 걸렸을 때는 운동을 완전히 쉬어야 한다.
운동을 쉬었다가 다시 시작할 때는 예전보다 낮은 강도에서 시작해 조금씩 늘려야 한다.
B.explain_ko: 쉬었다 돌아오면 예전의 절반쯤으로 시작해 매주 조금씩 늘리라는 것이 핵심이다. 감기·5킬로미터는 예로 나온 말일 뿐이고, 준비 운동은 말하지 않았다.

B.question: 다음 상황 설명을 듣고, Ivy가 Mr. Cole에게 할 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
B.script: W: Ivy is a volunteer at her neighborhood's clothing swap, an event where people trade clothes they no longer wear instead of throwing them away. The rule is simple. People can bring up to five pieces of clothing that are clean and in good condition, and they can take the same number home. This afternoon, a man named Mr. Cole arrives with a large bag. When Ivy checks it, she finds that most of the shirts have holes or stains that won't come out. She doesn't want to embarrass him, but she can't put these clothes on the tables. Then she remembers the textile recycling box at the entrance of the hall, where damaged clothes are collected and made into cleaning cloths. In this situation, what would Ivy most likely say to Mr. Cole?
choices: You can bring up to five pieces of clothing and take the same number home.
I'm sorry, but we can only take clean clothes in good shape. You could put these in the recycling box at the entrance.
Thank you! These shirts will be really popular at today's swap.
Why don't you just throw these shirts in the trash can over there?

B.passage: My pen pal, Aino, lives in Finland. Last week, she sent me a letter and a photo. Every February, her town has a snow festival. People make big animals out of snow, and children slide down the hills. This year, Aino and her dad made a snow bear. It was taller than her dad! At the end of her letter, she wrote, "Snow is _____ here in winter, so please visit me!"
B.question: Which best fits in the blank?
B.explain_ko: 눈 축제가 열리는 곳이니 겨울에 눈이 어디에나(everywhere) 있다며 놀러 오라고 한다.

B.passage: Do you know how children played one hundred years ago? At Dasom Toy Museum, you can find out. The museum has more than two thousand old toys, such as wooden tops, paper dolls, and tin cars. Most of them were made by hand at home. You cannot touch the toys in the glass boxes, but you can play with the toys in the play room. On the second floor, visitors can make their own simple toys, like a paper doll. The museum is open every day except Mondays.
B.question: 이 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: A Museum Full of Old Toys
How to Make a Paper Doll
B.explain_ko: 옛날 장난감을 모아 둔 박물관을 소개하는 글이다.

2층에서 간단한 장난감을 직접 만들 수 있다.

B.passage:
Last summer, my family went camping by a lake for the first time.
(A) After dinner, we sat around the fire and roasted marshmallows. Then we looked up at the sky. There were so many stars!
(B) The next morning, I woke up early because of the birds. I walked to the lake with my sister and saw fish jumping out of the water.
(C) When we arrived, Dad and I put up the tent. It was harder than I thought, but we did it together. Mom made a fire for dinner.
B.question: 주어진 첫 문장 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 알맞은 것은?
B.explain_ko: When we arrived(C) → After dinner(A) → The next morning(B).

B.passage: Every day, people throw away a lot of plastic bottles. But many of them are never recycled because people throw them out the wrong way. Recycling a bottle is easy if you follow three simple steps. First, empty the bottle and wash it with water. Second, take off the label, because the label is made of a different kind of plastic. Third, press the bottle flat and put the cap back on. Then put it in the plastic bin, not the general trash. When bottles are clean and in the right bin, factories can turn them into new things like clothes, bags, and shoes. So a small effort at home can make a big _____ for our planet.
B.question: 이 글의 주제로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 플라스틱 병 대신 유리병을 써야 하는 이유
집에서 쓰레기를 줄이는 여러 가지 습관
플라스틱 병을 올바르게 분리 배출하는 방법
B.explain_ko: 플라스틱 병을 재활용되게 내놓는 세 단계를 설명하는 글이다.

B.question: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은?
B.explain_ko: 집에서의 작은 노력이 지구에 큰 차이(difference)를 만든다.

B.passage: Do you love animals? Hanul Animal Shelter is looking for volunteers this winter. We take care of about forty dogs and cats that have no home. Every day, they need food, clean water, and a warm place to sleep. They also need people to play with them and take them for walks. Volunteers will help us feed the animals, clean their rooms, and walk the dogs. You must be at least twelve years old, and students under fifteen should come with a parent. We are open from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. every Saturday and Sunday. If you are interested, please call us at 031-555-2040. The animals are waiting for you!
B.question: 이 글을 쓴 목적으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 집 없는 동물을 입양해 달라고 부탁하려고
동물 보호소의 문 여는 시간이 바뀐 것을 알리려고
보호소에 동물 먹이를 기부해 달라고 요청하려고
B.explain_ko: Hanul Animal Shelter is looking for volunteers → 자원봉사자 모집 광고이다.

B.question: 밑줄 친 부분의 소리가 다른 것은?
B.explain_ko: nose 의 o 는 [오우], 나머지는 짧은 [아].

B.question: 밑줄 친 부분의 소리가 다른 것은?
B.explain_ko: school 의 ch 는 [ㅋ], 나머지는 [취].

B.question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
There _____ a cat on the sofa.
B.explain_ko: a cat(단수) 앞에는 There is.

B.question:
대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
A: Can your sister ride a bike?
B: No, she _____. She is only three.
B.explain_ko: Can 으로 물으면 can / can't 로 답한다.

B.question:
대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
A: What did you eat for breakfast?
B: I _____ some toast and milk.
B.explain_ko: did 로 물은 과거 → eat 의 과거형 ate (불규칙).

B.question:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
My bag is _____ than yours.
B.explain_ko: than 앞은 비교급, y 로 끝나면 y 를 i 로 → heavier.

B.question: [study] 알맞은 꼴로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.explain_ko: 3인칭 단수 현재, 자음 + y 는 y 를 i 로 바꾸고 -es → studies

B.question: [do not] 과거 부정의 줄임말로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: We {} have P.E. class last Friday.
B.explain_ko: 과거 부정 did not → 줄임말 didn't + 동사원형 have

B.question: [write] 알맞은 꼴로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: Be quiet! My brother {} {} a letter.
B.explain_ko: 현재진행 is + writing (e 를 빼고 -ing)

B.question: [buy] 알맞은 꼴로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: Mom {} a new bag for me last week.
B.hint_ko: [엄마는 지난주에 나에게 새 가방을 사 주셨다.]
B.explain_ko: last week → 과거, buy 의 불규칙 과거 bought

B.question: [live] 알맞은 꼴로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.explain_ko: since + 과거 시점 → 계속의 현재완료 has + lived

B.question: 우리 엄마는 매일 아침 달리신다. (run, every, morning)
B.explain_ko: My mom runs every morning. 3인칭 단수 현재 runs

B.question: 내 남동생은 자전거를 탈 수 있다. (can, ride, bike)
B.explain_ko: My brother can ride a bike. can + 동사원형

B.question: 너는 지난 일요일에 무엇을 했니? (what, do, last, Sunday)
B.explain_ko: What did you do last Sunday? 일반동사 과거 의문문 did + 주어 + 동사원형

B.question: 우리는 할머니를 찾아뵙기 위해 기차를 탔다. (take, train, visit, grandmother)
B.explain_ko: We took a train to visit our grandmother. '~하기 위해'(목적) → to부정사

A.question: [teach] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: Ms. Park {} us how to make kimchi last Friday.
A.hint_ko: [박 선생님은 지난 금요일에 우리에게 김치 만드는 법을 가르쳐 주셨다.]
A.explain_ko: last Friday → 과거. teach 의 과거형은 불규칙 taught

A.question: [lie] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: When I got home, my cat {} {} on the sofa.
A.hint_ko: [내가 집에 왔을 때, 고양이는 소파에 누워 있었다.] (과거진행형)
A.explain_ko: 과거진행 was + -ing. lie 는 ie 를 y 로 바꿔 lying

A.question: [write] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: This letter {} {} by my grandmother fifty years ago.
A.hint_ko: [이 편지는 50년 전에 우리 할머니가 쓰셨다.] (과거 시제)
A.explain_ko: 편지가 쓰인 것이므로 수동태 be + 과거분사. 과거라서 was written

A.question: [leave] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: When we arrived at the station, the train {} already {}.
A.hint_ko: [우리가 역에 도착했을 때, 기차는 이미 떠나 버렸었다.]
A.explain_ko: 도착한 과거보다 더 먼저 일어난 일 → 과거완료 had + left

A.question: [danger] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: The heavy snow made the mountain road {}.
A.explain_ko: make + 목적어 + 형용사(목적격 보어). 명사 danger → 형용사 dangerous

A.question: [who] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: I have a friend {} father is a firefighter.
A.explain_ko: friend 의 아버지 → 소유격 관계대명사 whose

A.question: [know] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: If I {} {} your phone number, I would have called you.
A.hint_ko: [내가 네 전화번호를 알았더라면, 너에게 전화했을 텐데.]
A.explain_ko: 과거 사실의 반대 → If + had + 과거분사, would have + 과거분사

A.question: [do] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
A.template: Rarely {} my father come home before nine.
A.hint_ko: [우리 아버지는 9시 전에 집에 오시는 일이 거의 없다.] (현재 시제)
A.explain_ko: 부정어 Rarely 가 앞에 오면 도치 → 조동사 does + 주어 + 동사원형

A.question: 이것은 50년 전에 지어진 다리이다. (bridge, build, years, ago)
A.explain_ko: This is a bridge built 50 years ago. 과거분사 built 가 뒤에서 bridge 를 꾸민다

A.question: 위에서 보면, 그 섬은 하트처럼 보인다. (see, above, island, look, heart)
A.explain_ko: Seen from above, the island looks like a heart. 섬이 '보이는' 것이므로 수동 분사구문 (Being) Seen

A.question: 그 상자가 너무 무거워서 들 수 없으면, 우리는 아빠께 도움을 청할 것이다. (box, heavy, lift, ask, Dad, help)
A.explain_ko: If the box is too heavy to lift, we'll ask Dad for help. 조건절은 현재 시제, too + 형용사 + to부정사 = 너무 ~해서 …할 수 없다

B.question: [catch] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: My uncle {} a huge fish at the lake last Sunday.
B.hint_ko: [우리 삼촌은 지난 일요일에 호수에서 커다란 물고기를 잡으셨다.]
B.explain_ko: last Sunday → 과거. catch 의 과거형은 불규칙 caught

B.question: [swim] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: At 3 p.m. yesterday, the children {} {} in the river.
B.hint_ko: [어제 오후 세 시에, 아이들은 강에서 수영하고 있었다.] (과거진행형)
B.explain_ko: 과거진행 were + -ing. swim 은 단모음 + 단자음이라 m 을 한 번 더 써서 swimming

B.question: [hold] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: The school festival {} {} in the gym last Saturday.
B.hint_ko: [학교 축제는 지난 토요일에 체육관에서 열렸다.] (과거 시제)
B.explain_ko: 축제가 '열린' 것이므로 수동태 be + 과거분사. 과거라서 was held (hold-held-held)

B.question: [lose] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: Oh no! I {} {} my wallet, so I can't pay for this now.
B.hint_ko: [이런! 지갑을 잃어버려서 지금 이걸 계산할 수가 없어.] (현재완료)
B.explain_ko: 잃어버린 결과가 지금까지 이어짐 → 현재완료 have + 과거분사 lost

B.question: [health] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: Walking every day keeps your heart {}.
B.explain_ko: keep + 목적어 + 형용사(목적격 보어). 명사 health → 형용사 healthy

B.question: [who] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: The boy with {} I shared my umbrella is in my class.
B.hint_ko: [내가 우산을 같이 쓴 그 남자아이는 우리 반이다.]
B.explain_ko: shared my umbrella with the boy → 전치사 with 뒤의 목적격 관계대명사는 whom (전치사 바로 뒤에는 who·that 을 쓰지 않는다)

B.question: [bring] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: If you {} {} a map, we would not have gotten lost.
B.hint_ko: [네가 지도를 가져왔더라면, 우리는 길을 잃지 않았을 텐데.]
B.explain_ko: 과거 사실의 반대 → If + had + 과거분사(brought), would have + 과거분사

B.question: [do] 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰세요.
B.template: Little {} Minsu know that his friends were planning a party for him.
B.hint_ko: [민수는 친구들이 자기를 위해 파티를 준비하고 있다는 것을 전혀 몰랐다.] (과거 시제)
B.explain_ko: 부정어 Little 이 앞에 오면 도치 → 조동사 did + 주어 + 동사원형 know

B.question: 빨간 모자를 쓰고 있는 남자가 우리 코치님이다. (man, wear, red, cap, coach)
B.explain_ko: The man wearing a red cap is our coach. 현재분사 wearing 이 이끄는 말이 뒤에서 man 을 꾸민다

B.question: 열쇠가 없어서, 나는 집 밖에서 기다렸다. (not, have, key, wait, outside, house)
B.explain_ko: Not having a key, I waited outside the house. 이유를 나타내는 분사구문, 부정어 not 은 분사 앞에 둔다

B.question: 수영할 수 있을 만큼 날씨가 따뜻하면, 우리는 해변에 갈 것이다. (it, warm, enough, to, swim, go, beach)
B.explain_ko: If it is warm enough to swim, we'll go to the beach. 조건절은 미래라도 현재 시제, 형용사 + enough + to부정사 = …할 만큼 충분히 ~한
